catalog_quote: Stress Words with more than one syllable usually have the stress on the penultimate syllable. If the root has only one syllable, and the word has a prefix, the stress is on the prefix. [ˈipox] ‘su barriga’ [ˈnowan] ‘with me’ [ˈipan] ‘above it’ There are some postfixes that are not counted, though, like the absolutive suffix –tli, locative suffix -co, plural suffix –ten, and –qui which makes verbs into nouns. When a word ends on these postfixes, the stress is on the antepenultimate syllable. [ˈmaht͡ɬakt͡ɬiʔ] ‘five’ [ˈtilmaht͡ɬiʔ] ‘cloth’ [aˈjohwit͡ʃtliʔ] ‘squash seed’ [t͡ɬaˈtzokwelkoʔ] ‘place where the soil is uneven’ [t͡ɬahˈpijalten] ‘domestic animals / horses’ [ˈtⁱopiʃkiʔ] ‘sacerdote’, lit. ‘templehaver’ [t͡ʃiˈbohpiʃkiʔ] ‘sheperd’, lit. ‘goathaver’, Words borrowed from Spanish that do not have penultimate accent in Spanish do carry penultimate accent in SMT Nahuatl, like [ˈdoktor] ‘doctor’ [ˈkahfen] ‘café’ [ˈkolal] ‘corral’ [ˈbiskal] ‘fiscal’ [ˈrelok] [ˈrelos] ‘reloj’ [printed p. 18:] because the stress is always on the penultimate syllable in Nahuatl ... [printed p. 19:] the stress is on the second i, because it is the nucleus of the penultimate syllable, which is regularly stressed in Náhuatl. ... [printed p. 27:] stress adaptation, loans are stressed on the penultimate syllable: doctor [‘doctor] café [‘kajben] / [‘kajfen] Gaspar [‘Gaspar] reloj [‘relok] / [‘relos] Zacatlán [saˈkatlan]

[ˈipox] 'su barriga' [ˈnowan] 'with me' [ˈipan] 'above it'; then on printed p. 22: 'There are some postfixes that are not counted, though, like the absolutive suffix –tli, locative suffix -co, plural suffix –ten, and –qui which makes verbs into nouns. When a word ends on these postfixes, the stress is on…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word (counting prefixes: a monosyllabic root with a prefix is stressed on the prefix). A closed set of final suffixes — absolutive -tli, locative -co, plural -ten, agentive -qui — is extrametrical, so words ending in them are stressed on the antepenult (i.e., on the penult of the base). Spanish loans are re-stressed to the penult. Elsewhere in the same ms. (p. 18-19) the author uses the rule that 'the stress is always on the penultimate syllable in Nahuatl' to decide vowel-length/syllabification questions.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned. (p. 21: a reduplicated vowel sequence is 'audibly two syllable nucleuses, receiving two stresses', versus one long vowel.)
new_statements.exceptions: Final -tli, -co, -ten, -qui not counted (stress on antepenult); prefix stressed when root is monosyllabic; Spanish loans shifted to penultimate stress (doctor, café, corral, fiscal, reloj). Hedged with 'usually'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (phonological word including prefixes), citation forms in phonetic transcription; draft manuscript 'posted as is without peer review'. The variety described is that of San Miguel Tenango (municipio de Zacatlán), which SIL/ISO treat as the reference lect of nhi.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement source describes the Nahuatl of San Miguel Tenango, municipio de Zacatlán, Puebla ('SMT Nahuatl'), which SIL and ISO 639-3 treat as the reference lect of nhi (Ethnologue alternate name 'Tenango Nahuatl'; Glottolog zaca1241, no child languoids). It does not cover the Ahuacatlán or Tepetzintla villages directly. Glottolog's ref 547285 'Bartholomew, Doris (n.d.), Gramática del Náhuatl de San Miguel Tenango' is the same SIL manuscript now catalogued as Schroeder 2014 (the 'Bartholomew Collection' is the archive series name, not the author). Brockway 1963/1979 'North Puebla Nahuatl' (Naupan) belongs to Northern Puebla Nahuatl [ncj] (Glottolog nort2957), not to this language.

new_statements.quote: [p. 27] Los prefijos y los posfijos tienen un orden establecido, y otras palabras no pueden aparecer en medio de ellos. El acento de una palabra cae en la penúltima sílaba. La mayoría de los sufijos tienen nada más un sentido gramatical. [p. 105] Para mantener el patrón silábico permitido (CVC como máximo) se introduce una i antes o después del prefijo-consonante, formando así una sílaba. En la mayoría de los casos esta sílaba no lleva acento, y entonces la i se introduce antes de la consonante, e.g. itkimpiya, inkowa, iktlalia. Sin embargo, si la sílaba que lleva el prefijo-consonante lleva acento se introduce la i después del consonante, e.g. kikwa, okipix, niyoj, tikaj. Compare las mismas radicales cuando la sílaba del prefijo-consonante lleva el acento y cuando no lo lleva (el acento siempre va en la penúltima sílaba): ikpixtok 'está teniendo' / okipix 'tuvo'; ikkwajtok 'está comiendo' / kikwas 'comerá'
new_statements.translation: [p. 27] The prefixes and postfixes have a fixed order, and other words cannot appear between them. The stress of a word falls on the penultimate syllable. Most suffixes have only a grammatical meaning. [p. 105] To keep the permitted syllable pattern (CVC at most) an i is inserted before or after the prefix-consonant, thus forming a syllable. In most cases this syllable does not carry stress, and then the i is inserted before the consonant, e.g. itkimpiya, inkowa, iktlalia. However, if the syllable carrying the prefix-consonant carries stress, the i is inserted after the consonant, e.g. kikwa, okipix, niyoj, tikaj. Compare the same stems when the syllable of the prefix-consonant carries the stress and when it does not (the stress always goes on the penultimate syllable): ikpixtok 'is having' / okipix 'had'; ikkwajtok 'is eating' / kikwas 'will eat'

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog penultimate stress (penultimate) and as the existing Schroeder 2015 Phonology statement. It adds the epenthesis diagnostic showing that a consonant-only prefix syllable is stressed exactly when it is penultimate (kikwa, okipix vs. iktlalia, ikpixtok), i.e. the stress domain includes the prefixes, as the phonology's [ˈipox] example already implied; it does not repeat the phonology's remark that some postfixes are not counted.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the (prefix+root+suffix) word; the grammar says 'always'. Stress position is diagnosed by epenthesis in consonant-only subject/object prefixes: an epenthetic i goes before the prefix consonant when that syllable is unstressed (it-, in-, ik-) and after it when the syllable is the stressed penult (ki-, ni-, ti-), so ik-pix-tok vs. o-ki-pix.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated in the grammar (it says the stress 'siempre' goes on the penult). Note the example oniktzakw 'la cerré' glossed 'stressed n- becomes ni-, not in-' (p. 106), consistent with the penult rule. The grammar has no phonology chapter; the two passages are asides in the morphology.
new_statements.identity_note: Both works describe the Nahuatl of San Miguel Tenango, municipio de Zacatlán, Puebla (ISO nhi, Zacatlán-Ahuacatlán-Tepetzintla Nahuatl), the same variety the catalog entry names; the SIL records list the subject language as nhi. Glottolog's reference 547285 credits 'Bartholomew, Doris, n.d.' for the grammar; that is the collection name (Bartholomew Collection of Unpublished Materials), the author is Petra Schroeder.

new_statements.relation_note: The held English original IS the catalog record's source (catalog quote = this document's 'Stress' section verbatim, same locator); penultimate fixed stress with the -tli/-co/-ten/-qui antepenult exceptions, matching catalog penultimate stress and both existing_statements (Schroeder 2015 Phonology; Schroeder 2014 Gramática p. 27 'El acento de una palabra cae en la penúltima sílaba'). The Spanish translation (62739) was not seen, so nothing new is added beyond confirming the duplicate.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is regular and non-contrastive: it falls on the penultimate syllable of the word. Stated exceptions: (i) a monosyllabic root with a prefix is stressed on the prefix (which is still the penult of the disyllable, e.g. [ˈipox]); (ii) a set of 'uncounted' final suffixes (absolutive -tli, locative -co, plural -ten, nominalizer -qui) leave stress on the antepenult of the surface word, i.e. penult of the stem without them; (iii) Spanish loans are re-stressed to the penult ([ˈdoktor], [ˈkahfen] 'café'); the article in is never stressed and is treated as a separate word.
new_statements.secondary_stress: none described (the text mentions 'two stresses' only for a reduplicated-vowel sequence forming two syllable nuclei, PDF p. 22, not a secondary-stress system).
new_statements.exceptions: antepenultimate surface stress before the extrametrical suffixes -tli, -co, -ten, -qui ([ˈmaht͡ɬakt͡ɬiʔ] 'five', [ˈtilmaht͡ɬiʔ] 'cloth', [t͡ɬahˈpijalten] 'domestic animals'); prefix stressed when the root is monosyllabic; loans adapted to penult stress; unstressed article; epenthetic i placed before/after a consonantal prefix depending on whether that syllable carries stress (PDF p. 25).
new_statements.identity_note: The work describes Nahuatl de San Miguel Tenango ('SMT Nahuatl'), municipio of Zacatlán, Puebla = the reference lect of ISO nhi (Zacatlán-Ahuacatlán-Tepetzintla Nahuatl), Glottolog zaca1241; title page and running text name only San Miguel Tenango.
